newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Berri gas plant starts commissioning.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Berri gas plant starts commissioning.

text.p: Commissioning has begun at the expanded Berri gas processing plant in Saudi Arabia's master gas system (MGS), Gulf industry sources said on Monday.

Berri is part of state-oil firm Saudi Aramco's programme to keep pace with surging domestic gas demand from power and petrochemical firms in the kingdom by expanding the capacity of the MGS system which has run up against capacity constraints.
"It (Berri) is 99 percent complete...It's in various stages of start-up right now, in pre-commissioning and commissioning," said a regional industry source.

The completed work at Berri, north-east of Riyadh, will allow the revamped plant to process approximately one billion cubic feet a day of gas compared to 750 million cubic feet previously within a month, the industry sources said.
A second expansion of Berri, to handle an additional 250 million cubic feet, is also out to tender, the sources said.

Aramco is also carrying out work to debottleneck its Shedgum and Uthmaniyah processing plants on the MGS and last year issued tenders to build a new $2 billion gas plant at Hawiyah also in the populous Eastern Province.

Total electric power demand in Saudi Arabia will grow at an average rate of 4.5 percent till 2020, Saudi Minister of Industry and Electricity Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani told a conference last week.
